content.title: Route per-kind Turn behavior through turnBehavior
content.intent: This PR is a refactor. One table, turnBehavior, now decides each Turn's prompt mode, tools, delivery and answer gate from Conversation kind and opener. A lint rule blocks new scattered branches.

chapters.caption: One table maps kind and opener to Turn behavior
chapters.body: turnBehavior returns one of four fixed rows: root, person in a Thread, agent in a child, and Automation run [1]. The check order picks the row: Automation run first, then root, then the opener [2]. isPersonInput, once copied in two files, now lives here and counts only Slack and web input [3].

decisions.claim: A temporary automationRun flag is a fine stand-in until Conversation kind automation exists.
decisions.concern: The flag still comes from dispatch.declaresResult, so the old signal stays on the hot path until a later PR removes it.

asks: Why does an Automation run win over the kind check?

chapters.caption: executeAgentRun computes the behavior once and hands it down
chapters.body: executeAgentRun now builds the behavior from the kind, the Source and the dispatch, and takes the Automation gate from it [1]. assemblePrompt used to work out the prompt mode from declaresResult and agentInvocationId; it now receives it as an argument [2][3]. Tool wiring puts behavior.tools on the tool context in place of agentInvocationId [4].
asks: Does the prompt mode match the old one for every kind?

chapters.caption: spawnAgent and messageAgent binding moves into tool wiring
chapters.body: createAgentRunner used to bind both agent tools up front, keyed on agentInvocationId [1]. Now it only passes the binders through [2]. bindAgentTools decides from the Turn's agents value, so a too-deep child can still message its parent [3]. A person's Thread Turn used to block spawning with a subagents flag; agents none does that now [4].
asks: Does anything else still read durability.spawnAgent?

chapters.caption: Tool gates read turnTools instead of agentInvocationId
chapters.body: createTools now adds reportBlocked and noReply from turnTools flags. It used to check agentInvocationId and use an if/else around the Automation tool [1]. The review desk's disabled reason [2], subscriptions [3] and user customization [4] switch the same way.
asks: Is noReply still absent for an Automation run?

chapters.caption: Event delivery and run-notice helpers move into the module
chapters.body: The Event Turn worker used to deliver to the Location only for kind root. It now asks the table, which gives the same answer for a non-person opener [1]. deliversFinalText and postsRunNotices moved out of automation-result.ts unchanged [2][3], and the Slack resume and turn paths import them from the new module.

chapters.caption: Unit tests pin each row and each binding case
chapters.body: A new unit test checks the full behavior row for each kind and opener, the task throw, and the Automation row [1]. Binding tests cover agents none, both spawn values, and the too-deep child that keeps messageAgent [2]. An eval checks that a person's reply in an Automation run's thread runs as a chat Turn and does not call finishAutomationRun [3].

decisions.claim: Row tests are enough proof that no behavior changed.
decisions.concern: The tests check the new table, not that each old branch gave the same result, so a changed case such as an Event Turn in a Thread is not caught.

asks: Is there a test for an Event Turn in a Thread?

chapters.caption: Two new throws reject states the old code allowed
chapters.body: executeAgentRun now fails a child Run that has no Conversation row. Before, it ran with an undefined kind [1]. turnBehavior throws when a person's input reaches a task Conversation [2]. Both assume these states cannot happen in production.

decisions.claim: A child Run without a row and person input on a task never happen, so throwing is safe.
decisions.concern: A spawn race or a legacy row could hit these paths and now fails the Turn instead of running it.

asks: What happens to a Turn that hits these throws?

chapters.caption: A non-person Turn in a Thread now runs as a child agent
chapters.body: Every non-person Turn on a child now gets the agent-in-child row [1]. Before, only a Run with agentInvocationId got child-agent mode [2], and every Thread Turn had subagents disabled [3]. So, inferred from the code, an Event Turn in a Thread now gets the child_agent prompt and reportBlocked, loses the review desk, and can spawn agents.

decisions.claim: An Event Turn in a Thread should behave like an agent invocation, not like a person's Turn.
decisions.concern: The PR says no behavior change. A watch that a person set in a Thread now wakes a Turn with different tools and prompt, and it can spawn agents.

asks: Can an Event reach a Thread today?
Was this change intended for the child-agent series?

chapters.caption: A source lint rule confines kind branches to kind-behavior.ts
chapters.body: A new kind-behavior rule counts branches on kind, person Source, declaresResult, and parent-edge fields in runtime source [1]. It runs over packages/junior/src with the shared baseline [2]. The baseline lists the legacy sites, so each count can only go down [3]. Tests cover the matched and ignored forms [4].

decisions.claim: A regex count is strict enough to stop new kind branches.
decisions.concern: A branch through a helper or an alias passes the regex. The error text forbids that, but nothing enforces it.

asks: Why a regex instead of an AST check?

splits.reason: Mixes the turnBehavior refactor with a new lint rule and baseline in scripts/; the rule could ship on its own.
